Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Ordnance Production Manager in the Production Department at the Navy Submarine Torpedo Facility (NSTF) of NAVSUBTORP FAC.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will supervise a diverse team of government civilian and military personnel, exercising managerial authority to achieve the goals of the MK48 Intermediate Maintenance Activity (IMA).
You will exercise direct supervisory authority to plan, direct, coordinate, and assess work, ensuring the effective and expeditious execution of the Production Department's goals and schedules.
You will manage the planning, maintenance, and delivery of MK 48 Heavyweight Torpedoes, establishing short- and long-term objectives to meet fleet delivery dates and customer expectations.
You will serve as a torpedo production advisor to the Commanding Officer, setting departmental policies and ensuring effective execution of production schedules.
You will plan and manage resources, including equipment, material, and manpower, and resolve conflicts between customer demands and Intermediate Maintenance Activity (IMA) capacity.
You will analyze and evaluate production operations, researching and implementing improved business practices to eliminate bottlenecks and optimize workflow.

You will serve as a Technical Assistant for NAVSEA service contracts by defining contract requirements, monitoring contractor deliverables, and providing performance assessment reports to the Contracting Officer's Representative.

You will provide comprehensive technical and management advisory assistance to subordinate supervisors and personnel on troubleshooting complex electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic components of the MK 48 ADCAP torpedo.
You will analyze failure trends, investigate process or safety deficiencies, and implement corrective action plans to enhance torpedo maintenance quality and reliability.
You will manage the preventive maintenance program for all machinery, test equipment, and ordnance handling equipment used in explosive torpedo loading, repair, rework, and handling.
You will identify training and developmental needs, monitor classroom and on-the-job training, and evaluate training systems to ensure a highly qualified, cross-trained, and flexible workforce.
You will manage hiring actions, promotions, training, and employee recognition.
You will interpret and enforce explosive safety and security regulations (including NAVSUP P-805 and NAVSEA OP5).
You will perform other related duties as assigned by the Production Department to support the overall operational readiness of the Submarine Fleet.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-12 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Managing a comprehensive facilities maintenance program. This experience must include: Supervising a diverse workforce of trades personnel executing maintenance, repair, and construction activities across various crafts. Utilizing a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) for the planning, scheduling, and execution of work. Developing and implementing maintenance strategies and policies, preventative maintenance programs, and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) program. Overseeing customer service operations to resolve complaints and ensure responsive support for all stakeholders. Managing the fiscal aspects of a facilities program, including developing budget estimates and tracking expenses to ensure work stays within approved funding limits. Serving as a senior advisor or technical expert on facilities management. This experience must demonstrate the ability to direct complex work, manage competing priorities under pressure, and apply in-depth knowledge of facility management principles and practices to ensure the effective operation, maintenance, and preservation of infrastructure. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/1600/facility-operations-services-series-1640/ Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as the Facilities Maintenance Branch Chief, providing leadership, direction, and oversight for the installation’s comprehensive facilities maintenance and repair program.

You will plan, direct, coordinate, and evaluate facility maintenance and repair activities to ensure buildings, infrastructure, utilities, and supporting systems are maintained in a safe, reliable, and mission-ready condition.

You will manage preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, service calls, inspections, and repair programs, establishing priorities and allocating personnel, funding, equipment, and other resources to meet installation requirements.

You will supervise a multidisciplinary workforce responsible for facilities maintenance activities; establish performance expectations, assign work, evaluate performance, identify training needs, and promote workforce development and accountability.

You will develop short- and long-range maintenance plans and schedules, evaluate facility conditions and emerging requirements, and recommend priorities and courses of action to Public Works leadership.

You will manage facility maintenance resources and budgets, including development of funding requirements, monitoring execution, evaluating costs, and ensuring available resources are effectively applied to the highest-priority maintenance needs.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying. Qualification requirements emphasis is on quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the job elements and screen out listed below. This job has a screen-out element which will be used to determine minimum eligibility for this job. Applicants who do not receive a minimum of two points on the screen-out element(s) will be found ineligible. The Screen-out Element for this position is: ABILITY TO DO THE WORK OF THE POSITION WITHOUT MORE THAN NORMAL SUPERVISION: Performing common tasks including the ability to read and use technical manuals, illustrations, diagrams and schematics, and skill in the use of equipment and hand tools used for maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing generator equipment, automated and manual transfer switches, and auxiliary multi-fuel engine systems. Applicants must meet the requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Job Qualification Handbook for Trades and Labor Occupations. MajorDuties: You will inspect, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain generators, transfer switches, and related electrical systems.
You will maintain portable and stationary generators, ensuring readiness for emergency response.
You will install, modify, test, and repair electrical equipment, wiring, breakers, relays, and controls.
You will inspect and service mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and fuel systems.
You will monitor fuel levels, refuel equipment, and maintain fuel records.
You will comply with OSHA, NFPA, EPA, and environmental regulations while documenting work and maintaining a safe work area.
